shortDescription: Italy's manufacturing activity contracted in August for the first time in seven months, a survey showed on Tuesday, while cost pressures continued to ease.

children: Italy's manufacturing activity contracted in August for the first time in seven months, a survey showed on Tuesday, while cost pressures continued to ease.
The S&P Global Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index for the euro zone's third-largest economy fell to 49.6 from 51.3 in July, slightly below the 50 mark that separates growth from contraction.
A Reuters survey of nine analysts had pointed to a reading of 51.5.
The new orders subindex fell to 46.4 from 49.0 the month before, posting the lowest reading in almost a year and a half.
On the prices side, the subindex for input cost inflation tumbled in August to 64.1 from 69.1, while the indicator of output prices slipped to 56.4 from 57.7.
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government in April cut its economic growth outlook to 0.6% for this year and next from previous targets of 0.7% and 0.8% respectively.
